card.name: Pravo Horo
card.tagline: Bulgaria's most basic 'straight' national line dance.
card.profile: The 'straight/right' horo, a simple village line dance in 2/4 or 6/8 (counted 3+3) with a three-measure pattern (quick-quick-slow-slow). Dancers form concentric curving lines facing in, using a hand hold or belt hold (na lesa); the basic step dives toward the center and travels counter-clockwise. Regional styles vary - smooth in Thrace, sharp with lifted knees in the Shop region, earthy in Dobrudzha (where it is called Opas). Considered the national dance of Bulgaria (English Wikipedia; Eliznik).
card.insight: In Greek Thrace the same dance is called Zonaradiko; it is a staple of weddings and feast days and can continue for hours, the in-and-out motion becoming hypnotic (English Wikipedia).
card.image_significance: The line dance every Bulgarian knows. A representative image shows folk dress and patterned partner or group figures — national, Bulgaria.
